finding.guards_checked: Scheme must be http/https and a hostname must be present (validators.py:12). All resolved addresses checked against private, loopback, link-local, reserved ranges (validators.py:15-17). Redirects disabled (allow_redirects=False), so no Location-header re-fetch. Literal-IP and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms are blocked by the same check. Not closed: the check and the connection use separate DNS lookups (TOCTOU / DNS rebinding); response body is returned, so this is not blind.

verdict.guard_found: none. validators.py:12 checks only scheme and hostname presence. validators.py:14-17 resolves the host once and rejects private/loopback/link-local/reserved addresses, but this is not hostname membership, an anchored match, or a scheme-plus-allowlist check. views.py:14 then calls requests.get(url) with a second DNS lookup, and the validated IP is not pinned. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) blocks only redirect-based re-fetch, not rebinding.
verdict.reason: The source is the unauthenticated `url` query parameter (views.py:11), and the only check (validators.py:14-17) is an IP-range check on a separate DNS lookup, not a closing hostname or anchored-match guard, so views.py:14 can still be reached via DNS rebinding to a private address. The trace matches the code. Practical exploitation requires an attacker-controlled DNS name with a short TTL that flips between a public and a private address between the two lookups, so severity MEDIUM is reasonable. Separately, /fetch2 (views.py:19-22) has only a scheme check and is more directly exploitable, though it is not the candidate's sink.
